body: Own backtest (run 2026-11-20). Full population of Form 4 purchases from SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets; rule = >=2 distinct directors/officers buying (code P, not 10b5-1, price>=$1, common stock) within 30 days; dated on the filing day the 2nd buy became public, entry next trading day; one event per issuer per 365 days; mcap $300M-$10B (cover-page shares x insider price); SPACs/funds dropped, biotech separate. 849 usable non-biotech events (signals 2021-2024). Versus 5 size-matched random controls per event on the same date: 12m mean excess 0.0% (95% month-clustered bootstrap CI -4.8% to +5.0%), median -3.9%, hit rate 44.9%; 6m -0.3% (CI -3.3% to +2.6%). Versus IWM +1.7% 12m mean (CI -2.7% to +6.4%) but controls also beat IWM by +1.7%, so that is a size/survivor effect; versus SPY -7.9%. No subset was clean: $300M-$1B +4.8% 12m (CI -2.2 to +12.3), banks +4.0% at 6m (CI -2.5 to +10.0), >=3 insiders and CEO/CFO buys were worse, 2021 signals only year significantly positive (+6.3%). Survivorship: ~19% of eligible events lacked Yahoo data (SEC audit of 189: 162 acquired, 23 bankrupt); generous bound adds only ~+2%/yr. Lesson: the plain public cluster rule is not a standalone edge in this period; CMP-sized (~10%/yr) effect not reproduced without the opportunistic/routine filter. Use as a research-queue trigger only.

data.lesson: Public cluster screen = no standalone edge; at most a reason to research. Next test must pre-register opportunistic-only (CMP) + buy-size filter out of sample.

title: Backtest: US insider-buying clusters ($300M-$10B, 2021-2024) showed no excess return vs size-matched controls
